- **AC3:** README and key code comments (arena/engine/report) reflect the new default without stale skirmish-only claims.
- **AC4:** All related documentation is updated (code comments, `docs/BALANCING.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md`, README), with no stale skirmish-only claims remaining.
- **AC5:** The docs guards (`balancingDocs.test.ts`, `evaluationDocs.test.ts`) pass; no unrelated doc changes were made.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — fidelity boundary + batch/campaign semantics
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` — batch default, --skirmish, bounded budget, distribution reading
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`, `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` — code comments reflecting the boundary

# Limit the number of power-up slots

**Headline:** Cap the run's permanent power-up loadout at six kinds; once the six slots are full, only those power-ups (plus explicitly exempt entries such as Extra Life) may spawn or be offered as a permanent reward.

## Original request (verbatim)

> Currently the player can collect any number of powerups. This makes them way too powerful in late game. Limit the number of power-ups that can be collected to 6. The first 6 collected permanently (i.e. from the hull-full) become the only powerups the player can collect in that game. Once the 6 slots are full with permanent items no other powerup kind will spawn (a life powerup is an exception, there may be other exceptions later in the development cycles, so availability when full should become a flag on the powerup database entry). Until all 6 slots are full powerups will spawn as they do now.

> **Terminology:** the item text says "hull-full"; the shipped feature is the **hold-full choice** (`MineralChoiceScene`, driven by the mineral hold — GDD §4.5). This brief treats "hull-full" as "hold-full", i.e. a **permanent reward** grant. "Collected permanently" means a hold-full (or mini-boss upgrade) grant, never a field pickup.

## Problem statement

Players can currently collect every power-up kind in the catalogue, and every hold-full (permanent) reward can add a brand-new power-up kind with no upper bound. By the late game a player therefore owns every permanent effect at once, which makes the ship far too powerful and flattens the difficulty curve. The run needs a bounded loadout: the **first six distinct power-up kinds taken as permanent (hold-full) rewards** become the run's slots, and once all six slots are full no other power-up kind spawns or is offered as a new permanent pick.

## Users

- **Player (arcade run)** — wants a strong but bounded loadout, so late-game runs stay challenging and each run has a recognisable build identity.
- **Producer / designer** — wants the cap to be data-driven and tunable, with per-power-up exemptions (Extra Life today, more later) requiring no code change.
- **Agent / developer** — needs one shared implementation so the game and every gym behave identically (gym↔game parity).

### Example user stories

- As a player, once I have taken six permanent power-up rewards my build is fixed for the rest of the run, so my late-game ship is strong but no longer invincible.
- As a player with six full slots, the only power-ups I see are the six I chose (plus Extra Life), so every pickup I catch improves a power-up I actually own.
- As a designer, I can mark a power-up catalogue entry as available-when-full so a future exception (Extra Life today) needs data, not code.
- As an operator, I can observe the identical slot rule in the gyms as in the shipped game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Cap and accounting** — A single named, exported cap (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`) governs permanent power-up ownership; the number of occupied slots equals the count of distinct power-up ids with at least one permanent (hold-full) grant, read from the shared `PowerUpLevelStore` (`getLevels()` / `permanentGrants()`). Temporary field pickups and weapon grants do not occupy slots. A unit test proves the accounting (0 → 6 grants, repeats of an owned kind do not add a slot, weapon grants ignored).
2. **Spawn gating at full slots** — When all six slots are filled, the drop-selection path (game and gyms, one shared implementation) draws only from the six owned power-up ids plus every catalogue id flagged as available-when-full (Extra Life is flagged by default); every other power-up id is never drawn. Verified by a seeded/injected-rng unit test on the selection helper plus a `PlayScene` integration test that fills the slots and asserts a large sample of draws contains only owned/exempt ids.
3. **No behaviour change below the cap** — While fewer than six slots are filled, drop selection covers the full catalogue exactly as today: a regression test with a fixed rng seed produces the identical draw sequence before and after the change.
4. **Choice gating at full slots** — Once the slots are full, the hold-full (and mini-boss) choice offers level-ups of owned power-ups, available-when-full entries and weapons, but **no option that would create a seventh permanent power-up kind**; the candidate list degrades gracefully (weapon/level-up options still offered) and never returns a new power-up kind. Verified by choice-pool tests at 6 filled slots.
5. **Data-driven exemption** — The exemption is a flag on the power-up catalogue entry (`availableWhenSlotsFull`, default `false`), not an `id === 'extra_life'` special case; a test asserts Extra Life is exempt and every other catalogue entry defaults to non-exempt, so a new entry is non-exempt unless it opts in.
6. **Parity and run scope** — The rule lives once in shared core code consumed by `PlayScene` and the formation gyms (guard: `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` / parity tests); slot state is run-scoped and resets on run restart (`PowerUpLevelStore.reset()`). A parity/integration test proves the gym path and the game path consume the same gate.
7. **Documentation and suite** — The GDD (§4.4 catalogue table and §4.5 hold-full choice) and `docs/BALANCING.md` document the cap and the exemption flag; the full project test suite passes with the change.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1):** the rule must be implemented once in shared code (`src/powerups/*`, `src/scenes/core/*`) and consumed by `PlayScene` and the gyms. A gym may only diverge for a documented, disabled-feature reason — none is expected here.
- **Existing level semantics unchanged:** a repeat of an already-owned kind still levels it up (field pickup = temporary level, hold-full = permanent level).
- **Determinism:** selection must stay injectable-rng deterministic; no wall-clock or `Math.random()` reads inside the new pure helpers.
- **No catalogue removals and no weight retuning:** the cap is a gate on which ids may be drawn, not a rebalance of relative weights. Existing tuning rules (`GameRules.powerUpWeights`) keep their meaning for the ids that remain eligible.
- **Weapons are out of scope:** weapon drops, weapon unlocks and the mini-boss weapon unlock pool are unchanged except that the choice must still be able to offer them.

## Existing state

- **"Power-up database":** `src/powerups/types.ts` — `PowerUpEntry` / `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` (16 power-ups) and `POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS` in `src/core/rules.ts`; `WEAPON_DROP_IDS`/`CHOICE_POOL` list the weapon drops alongside.
- **Permanent ownership:** `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `PowerUpLevelStore.collect(id, permanent)`, `permanentGrants(id)`, `getLevels()` (permanent kinds only) and `getEffectiveLevel`/`getTempStacks` for temporary pickups.
- **Game spawn path:** `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_maybeDropPowerUp()` rolls the level-resolved drop chance, then spawns `this.dropSpawner.next()`. The spawner is built once by `buildDefaultDropSpawner()` (`src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts`) as a `WeightedRandomSpawner<DropId>` over `POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS + WEAPON_WEIGHT_IDS`, with weights from `src/core/rules.ts`. A small asteroid also rolls an additive deterministic `extra_life` drop (`PlayScene` §asteroid kill drops).
- **Gym spawn paths:** `GymFormationScene._spawnPowerUpDrop()` (`powerUpSpawner`), `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpLeveling`, `GymWeapons`, `GymLevel` — deterministic round-robin spawners.
- **Hold-full choice:** `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `CHOICE_POOL`, `buildChoiceCandidates()`, `drawWeightedWithoutReplacement()`, `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT`; `chooseOptions()` is consumed by `PlayScene` and every gym, and the mini-boss reward reuses `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions()` (`src/powerups/unlocks.ts`).
- **Effects application:** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect()` routes a collection to the store's temporary stack or permanent grant; no cap on distinct kinds exists today.
- **Docs of record:** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (catalogue/table) and §4.5 (hold-full choice), `docs/BALANCING.md` (drop/choice balance), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 (parity convention), `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`.

## Desired change

- Add `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6` (single named constant; see open question on location/persistence) and an `availableWhenSlotsFull` flag on `PowerUpEntry` (Extra Life `true`).
- Add a pure shared helper module (e.g. `src/powerups/slots.ts`) that, given the set of permanently-owned power-up ids and the catalogue, answers: slots used, slots free, and whether an id may be drawn/offered. It owns the exemption rule — no `id === 'extra_life'` branches anywhere else.
- Apply that helper at the two decision points, both shared with the gyms:
  1. **drop selection** (the weighted draw, so excluded ids are never selected while slots are full),
  2. **choice candidate construction** (`buildChoiceCandidates`, so no new permanent kind can be taken once full).
- Keep the below-cap path byte-for-byte equivalent in distribution (eligible set unchanged, weights unchanged).
- Cover with unit tests (helper + spawner + choice), integration tests (`PlayScene`), gym parity coverage, and documentation updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/types.ts` — add `availableWhenSlotsFull?: boolean` to `PowerUpEntry`; set `true` on `extra_life`; document default `false`.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6` (mirroring existing `POWER_UP_*` constants).
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` *(new)* + `src/powerups/slots.test.ts` — pure slot accounting and eligibility (exemptions included).
- `src/powerups/spawner.ts` — let a draw consult an eligibility predicate (or accept an eligible-id set) without weakening the all-zero-weight fallback.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` — `buildDefaultDropSpawner` / a shared `drawNextDrop(spawner, ownedIds)` seam so every scene draws through one filtered path.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — pass the run's permanently-owned power-up ids into the drop draw (and keep the asteroid `extra_life` path untouched).
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — filter brand-new power-up kinds out of `buildChoiceCandidates` at the cap (owned level-ups, exempt entries and weapons remain).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` / `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — expose the owned-permanent-kind view consumed by the two gates (no new counter).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — consume the same filtered draw path (no divergent copy).
- Tests: `src/powerups/slots.test.ts` (new), `src/powerups/spawner.test.ts`, `src/powerups/choice.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (parity guard).
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 catalogue table + §4.5 choice), `docs/BALANCING.md`, `README.md` if it states power-up rules.

## Related work

- AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P — *As the levels progress increase the number of enemies and decrease the number of power ups* (level-resolved drop chance; the supply-side counterpart of this demand-side cap).
- AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X — *Add level-scaling module and tunable rules* (where `powerUpDropChanceAtLevel1/Max` live; candidate home for a tunable cap).
- AH-0MV8GPGBL009M0D8 — *Smart Bomb is too powerful* (precedent for a single-power-up dominance fix; this item fixes dominance by accumulation instead).
- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 / AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR — power-up level curves and the `GymPowerUpLeveling` parity gym (the permanent-grant model this cap counts).
- AH-0MUTPEIZ5002FIJP — *P10 power-up identity — catalogue, spawn pool, choice pool and icon* (established that spawn pool and choice pool are catalogue-derived; the cap must not break that invariant).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity convention + duplicate-body guard.
- AH-0MVL9P2SF009QFON — shared level-up option builder used by hold-full choice and mini-boss reward (the choice gate must be applied at the shared builder seam, not duplicated).
- AH-0MUCST4M7008O9CX — *Pluggable power-up choice strategy and permanent-effect support* (the `ChoiceStrategy` seam the choice gate extends).
- AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV — *Feature: Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling* (precedent for permanent-grant semantics; weapons stay out of the slot cap).

## Risks and assumptions

- **All-zero-weight fallback:** `WeightedRandomSpawner` falls back to the first entry when every weight is zero, so exclusion must not be implemented by zeroing weights — it must be an eligibility filter applied before/while sampling.
- **Empty eligible set:** if the six owned kinds are all temporarily unavailable and exemptions are absent, the eligible power-up set must never be empty; the draw must degrade to weapons/exempt entries rather than crash or always return one id.
- **Test churn:** `src/core/rules.test.ts` and `src/powerups/choice.test.ts` assert the catalogue-complete pool; those assertions need an explicit "below cap" context.
- **Bot/balance evaluation drift:** `src/ai/eval/*` simulates campaigns and will see a different late-game loadout; the change may shift balance metrics. Re-recording bot evidence is *not* in scope unless a gate fails (record as a linked follow-up if needed).
- **Scope-creep risk:** HUD slot readout (`N/6`), persisting slots in checkpoints/saved runs, capping the mini-boss weapon unlock pool, and rebalancing individual power-up strength are all out of scope; each becomes a linked work item rather than extra scope here.
- **Assumption (A1):** a "slot" is a *distinct permanently-owned power-up kind*; weapons and temporary field pickups never consume one.
- **Assumption (A2):** the cap applies in the gyms as well as the game (parity); gyms are not exempted.
- **Assumption (A3):** no new player-facing HUD/UX surface is required by this item.
- **Assumption (A4):** the cap is a named code constant (default 6), not a persisted `GameRules` setting, unless the producer wants it runtime-tunable.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 (OPEN QUESTION)** — *Slot accounting:* does a slot represent a distinct permanently-owned power-up kind, so that weapons and temporary field pickups never occupy a slot? **Recommended:** yes — count only distinct power-up ids with at least one permanent (hold-full) grant; repeated grants of an owned kind level it up rather than consuming a new slot. *Status:* awaiting producer reply (auto-dispatched session; no interactive operator available).
- **Q2 (OPEN QUESTION)** — *Choice at the cap:* once the six slots are full, should the hold-full (and mini-boss) choice also stop offering brand-new power-up kinds — offering only level-ups of owned power-ups, available-when-full entries and weapons? **Recommended:** yes — otherwise a seventh permanent kind can be taken from the choice and the cap only affects spawning, which would be cosmetic. *Status:* awaiting producer reply.
- **Q3 (OPEN QUESTION)** — *Exemption flag and on-screen drops:* is `availableWhenSlotsFull` (default `false`, `true` for Extra Life) the right data-driven exemption, and what should happen to a drop of a non-owned kind that is already on screen when the sixth slot fills? **Recommended:** use that flag; already-spawned drops remain collectible for their temporary effect (they simply stop spawning). *Alternatives:* despawn them on the sixth grant, or block their collection. *Status:* awaiting producer reply.
- **Assumption A3 (unanswered, low risk):** no new HUD slot readout is required — if the producer wants an `N/6` indicator it should be an explicit AC or a linked follow-up item.
- **Assumption A4 (unanswered, low risk):** the cap ships as a named constant rather than a persisted `GameRules` field.
- **Research note:** duplicate-work check performed (`wl search` on "powerup slots limit", "powerup cap", "power-up limit", "spawn pool", "hold-full choice pool", "too powerful", "power creep") — no item (open or completed) implements a permanent loadout cap, so this item is not a duplicate. Closest completed work is the level-scaled power-up *supply* reduction (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P) and the Smart Bomb power reduction (AH-0MV8GPGBL009M0D8); both are related, neither covers loadout breadth.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUCST4M7008O9CX** – Pluggable power-up choice strategy and permanent-effect support (completed)
- **AH-0MUTPEIZ5002FIJP** – P10 power-up identity — catalogue, spawn pool, choice pool and icon (completed)
- **AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV** – Feature: Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, 0muv5clvq006v9hr, 0mv8gpgbl009m0d8, 0mvht1m6o003pu7p, 0mvl9p2sf009qfon (+492 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, 0muv5clvq006v9hr, 0mv8gpgbl009m0d8, 0mvht1m6o003pu7p, 0mvl9p2sf009qfon (+483 more)

## Intake questions for producer review

Intake for this item produced a full brief (problem statement, user stories, seven acceptance criteria, constraints, existing state, desired change, predicted key files, risks/assumptions — see the description) plus an automated related-work report. Three decisions are needed before the acceptance criteria can be frozen and the stage advanced. Each has a recommended option; reply with the option letter or your own wording.

### Q1 — What consumes a slot?

Does a "slot" mean a **distinct permanently-owned power-up kind**, so that weapon grants and temporary field pickups never occupy a slot?

- (a) **Distinct permanent power-up kinds only** — count `PowerUpLevelStore.getLevels()`; a repeat grant of an owned kind levels it up instead of taking a new slot; weapons and timed field pickups are ignored.
- (b) Distinct power-up kinds *including* field pickups — the first six power-up kinds the player ever touches are locked in, permanent or not.
- (c) Power-ups and weapons both consume slots from one shared pool of six.

**Recommended: (a)** — it matches the request's "collected permanently (i.e. from the hull-full)" wording, keeps the existing permanent/temporary level split untouched, and avoids rebalancing weapons as a side effect.

### Q2 — Does the hold-full choice also stop offering new kinds at the cap?

Once the six slots are full, should the hold-full choice (and the mini-boss reward) stop offering **brand-new power-up kinds**, offering only level-ups of owned power-ups, available-when-full entries (Extra Life) and weapons?

- (a) **Yes — gate the choice too.** The play run can never take a seventh permanent power-up kind; the only way to gain a power-up at the cap is to level one of the six or take an exempt entry.
- (b) No — only spawning is gated; the choice may still offer any power-up kind, and taking one would exceed six slots.

**Recommended: (a)** — with (b) the six-slot limit is cosmetic: the choice is the main permanent-grant path, so an unrestricted choice defeats the cap.

### Q3 — Exemption flag and drops already on screen

Is `availableWhenSlotsFull` (a boolean on the `PowerUpEntry` catalogue entry, default `false`, `true` for Extra Life) the right data-driven exemption — and what should happen to a drop of a non-owned kind that is already on screen when the sixth slot fills?

- (a) **Flag as named, and leave already-spawned drops collectible** for their temporary effect — they simply stop spawning from then on.
- (b) Flag as named, but despawn already-spawned non-owned drops the moment the sixth slot fills.
- (c) Flag as named, but leave already-spawned non-owned drops on screen and uncollectible (blocked at the collection gate).
- (d) Different flag name/semantics — please specify.

**Recommended: (a)** — it is the least surprising for the player (a drop you can see stays grabbable), needs no new collection gate, and the flag is the only data change a future exempt power-up needs.

### Assumptions recorded pending reply (correct them if wrong)

- **A3 — no new HUD surface.** The item does not add a slot counter/readout; if you want an `N/6` indicator, say so and it becomes an explicit AC (or a linked follow-up item).
- **A4 — code constant, not a setting.** The cap ships as a named exported constant (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`), not a persisted `GameRules` field, so it is not exposed in the rules/storage blob. Say so if you want it runtime-tunable.
- **A5 — gyms obey the cap.** The rule is shared core behaviour, so the gyms consume the same gate (gym↔game parity, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1); no gym is exempted.
- **A6 — out of scope.** HUD readout, checkpoint/save persistence of slots, capping the mini-boss weapon unlock pool, individual power-up rebalancing and re-recording bot-balance evidence are out of scope; each becomes a linked follow-up item if wanted.

**Duplicate-work check performed** — `wl search` across "powerup slots limit", "powerup cap", "power-up limit", "spawn pool", "hold-full choice pool", "too powerful" and "power creep": no open or completed item implements a permanent power-up loadout cap. Nearest work is the level-scaled power-up *supply* reduction (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P) and the Smart Bomb power reduction (AH-0MV8GPGBL009M0D8); both are related, neither overlaps this item's acceptance criteria.

Effort/risk estimation is deferred: the effort-and-risk skill gates on `stage` `intake_complete`/`plan_complete`, and the stage is intentionally held at `idea` until these questions are answered.

# Bot-batch force-field evidence (AC5, before/after)

Commands (deterministic, per-level campaign mode, competent policy, seeds 1–15):

```
node scripts/evaluate.mjs --batch --level 1  --force-fields on|off --games 15 --out /tmp/ff-evidence/l{1,5,10}-{on,off}
node scripts/evaluate.mjs --batch --level 5  --force-fields on|off --games 15 --out /tmp/ff-evidence/l{1,5,10}-{on,off}
node scripts/evaluate.mjs --batch --level 10 --force-fields on|off --games 15 --out /tmp/ff-evidence/l{1,5,10}-{on,off}
```

(`off` = hull-only pre-change baseline: fields resolved at level 1 → 0 hits for every shipped archetype; `on` = shipped `enemyForceFieldHits` curve.)

Aggregate means (per 15-game batch, `survivalSeconds` / `levelReached` / `avoidableHits` / `enemiesKilledByArchetype`):

| Level | Batch | survivalSeconds | levelReached | avoidableHits | enemiesKilledByArchetype (mean) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | off (baseline) | 67.76 | 1.00 | 3.00 | scout 15.13 |
| 1 | on | 67.76 | 1.00 | 3.00 | scout 15.13 |
| 5 | off (baseline) | 48.11 | 5.00 | 3.00 | phaser 9.33 |
| 5 | on | 33.00 | 5.00 | 3.00 | phaser 2.40 |
| 10 | off (baseline) | 11.55 | 10.00 | 3.00 | tank 7.27, diver 5.80, swarm 5.47, raider 0.13, ghost-* 0.13–0.53 |
| 10 | on | 12.50 | 10.00 | 3.00 | tank 1.33, diver 1.13, swarm 1.47, raider 0.07, ghost-* 0.13–0.33 |

**L1 unchanged:** the level-1 `runs.jsonl` on/off batches hash identically (`e6b2451348de6846`), so onboarding and the pre-change baseline are untouched (byte-identical gate satisfied).
